###chapter1
“Trust me! I’ll take care of you and make you the most honored woman in the world!”
The man’s firm promise echoed in her ears like a cruel joke, yet Elysia Thorne could only shake her head in panic. Before she could find the strength to resist, a sudden surge of force overwhelmed her, and the world went black under the weight of agonizing pain.
When she finally regained consciousness, the room was chillingly empty. The lingering scent of the chaos that had just occurred hung heavy in the air, and the disarray of her clothes told a silent, maddening tale.
She bit her lip until it bled, clutching the torn sheets as her vision blurred with hot, uncontrollable tears.
She was a married woman. She had come to the airport with a heart full of hope to finally meet her husband. But in the shadow of a dark lounge, amidst a confusion she still didn't understand, her virtue had been stolen before she could even see his face.
What does this mean? she thought, her mind spiraling. Is this infidelity? How can I ever face the world now? How can I face him?
If she told him the truth—that she had been dragged into the darkness while waiting for him—would he believe her? Would he still accept a wife who returned to him like this? Could a marriage that had never truly begun survive such a devastating blow?
Elysia wept for the life she had lost. She had grown up in a cold, loveless household, her destiny dictated by foster parents who saw her only as a bargaining chip. She had dreamed of escaping through education, but those dreams were crushed when she was forced to marry in her sister Daphne’s stead.
The groom, Tarquin Bradford, was rumored to be disabled, and her foster parents couldn't bear to see their biological daughter "suffer." So, they used years of obligation to coerce Elysia into a life she never asked for. From dropping out of college to signing the marriage papers, no one had ever asked if she was willing.
Yet, she had tried to make the best of it. They said marriage was a woman’s second chance at life, and for two years, she had been a faithful, invisible wife while Tarquin was abroad for treatment. She treasured this marriage because it was all she had left.
But today, the very day of his return, her world had shattered.
Her phone suddenly rang, jarring her back to the grim reality. It was the housekeeper.
“The master has asked for you to return immediately,” the woman said.
Elysia’s heart skipped a beat, her voice trembling. “Is he... is he home already?”
“Yes, ma’am. The master came looking for you, but when he saw you weren't there, he left. He wants you back at the villa to sign some documents. He... he is asking for a divorce.”
Elysia’s mind went blank, the news hitting her like a physical explosion.
Tarquin wanted a divorce?
She knew he was unhappy with the arranged marriage—he had been absent on their wedding day and distant ever since. In two years, they had never met face-to-face. Yet, he had provided for her every need, ensuring she was cared for even from across the ocean. She had thought that if she could just be a good wife, they could eventually build a life of quiet respect.
“Ma’am, you needn't be too upset,” the housekeeper added, her voice tinged with a strange excitement. “The master is being very generous. He’s left you the villa, two luxury cars, and a significant settlement.”
But as Elysia looked at her reflection in the darkened lounge, she realized that no amount of money could fix the woman staring back at her. She wasn't just losing a marriage; she was losing the last shred of hope she had for a clean start.

###chapter2
Elysia was on the brink of total despair. Her life felt like a relentless cycle of misfortune, but as she clutched the phone, she realized she had no right to refuse the divorce.
I have lost everything, she thought bitterly. I am no longer worthy of being his wife.
“I understand,” Elysia whispered, her voice hoarse and broken. “I’ll come home and sign the papers immediately.”
Fighting through her physical exhaustion and the heavy weight in her chest, she dressed with trembling hands and stumbled out of the terminal, disappearing into the crowded streets just as the world shifted around the airport.
No sooner had she vanished than a fleet of sleek black limousines swept toward the entrance. A troop of suited bodyguards emerged, forming a silent, impenetrable perimeter. The assistant stepped forward, opening the door with practiced reverence as Tarquin Bradford stepped out.
Exorbitantly priced bespoke tailoring, handcrafted leather shoes, and the cold glint of a limited-edition watch—Tarquin was the literal definition of power. His superior stature and striking features exuded an air of unattainable nobility, drawing the gaze of every onlooker, though none dared to breathe in his presence. He moved through the terminal with a regal authority, a man to be admired from a distance but never approached.
His mind was elsewhere. The previous night, he had been cornered by enemies after a compromised meal. In a moment of sheer desperation and clouded judgment, he had taken a young woman’s innocence in a dark corner of the airport lounge.
He had left in a hurry, fearing his pursuers would find her and use her against him. Now that the danger had been eliminated, he had returned to find her. He had made a promise in the heat of the night—a promise to take responsibility, to make her the happiest and most honored woman in the world.
Tarquin Bradford always kept his word.
Before he could reach the lounge, his assistant, Lowell, caught up to him, looking flustered. “Tarquin, there’s been a report from the villa. Your wife has returned, but... the housekeeper claims her behavior has been scandalous during your absence. There are marks on her today that suggest she wasn't alone last night. They say she has been seen with various men and has even spoken disparagingly about you in public.”
Tarquin’s face darkened, his eyes turning into shards of ice. “What did she say?”
Lowell hesitated. “She allegedly told people in a bar that you were... beneath her. That because of your injury, you were unworthy of her.”
“Hmph!” Tarquin’s lips curled into a cold, hard line.
His wife had been a pawn imposed on him by his family two years ago to curb his influence. He had never met her, not even on their wedding day. Now that he held absolute power, he was no longer bound by their games. His first act upon returning was to initiate a divorce—not out of cruelty, but because there was no love between them. He had intended to provide her with a billion-dollar settlement to ensure her future.
But if she was a woman of no virtue and no loyalty, she deserved nothing.
“The previous settlement is void,” Tarquin commanded, his voice frigid. “Rewrite it. She has been unfaithful and has disgraced the Bradford name. She will leave with nothing but the clothes on her back.”
“Yes, sir!”
Tarquin reached the lounge door. He took a breath, straightening his tie and smoothing his jacket. He wanted to show the young woman inside his most composed, gentlemanly side. Whatever the circumstances of their meeting, he was bound to her now by honor.
He pushed the door open.
The room was empty.
His brows furrowed in sudden, sharp frustration. Gone?
“Spread the word,” Tarquin barked to his men. “Find her. Use every resource at our disposal. I don't care about the cost—bring her to me!”
He would find the woman from the lounge. He would keep his promise. Little did he know, the "unfaithful" wife he had just condemned and the woman he was now desperately hunting were the very same person.

That’s why she had come to Jindale City–to find Tarquin and dissolve their marriage. 
She bore no grudge against Tarquin. She had wronged him first, and his accusations had not been entirely baseless. 
If she harbored any resentment, it was towards the man who had taken advantage of her that fateful night.
Men’s promises can be deceitful, and she had learned that the hard way. 
She had been told she would become the happiest and most honored woman in the world, but look how that turned out! 
Oh, the irony! 
Thinking about her past grievances… she felt a surge of anger! 
“Mommy, I gotta pee,” Emmett suddenly tugged at her clothes, his voice tinged with embarrassment. 
Elysia snapped back to the present, her gaze falling on her three kids. Her heart was immediately filled with warmth. 
The chaos of the past had indeed turned her life upside down, but it had given her these precious children, and for that, she was grateful.
